card.name: The q in dosing intervals
card.fires_on: The letter q at the start of a dosing-interval abbreviation such as q6h, q.d., q.i.d. or q 3 hours. It comes right after a dose in mg, often after a route like PO, IM or IV.

modes.label: q before hours
modes.description: q followed by a number of hours, written either joined or spaced.
modes.example: 15 mg PO, IM, or IV<< q>> 6 hours for 60 hours

modes.label: q with periods
modes.description: q in the Latin-style abbreviations q.d. and q.i.d. after a dose.
modes.example: a low dose of buspirone (eg, 2.5 mg<< q>>.d.) is recommended

card.writes: It promotes words meaning "each" or "every" (e.g. 每, 마다, 都有), which fits a repeat-interval reading.
card.plain: It fires on the "q" in "every X hours" dosing shorthand right after a dose amount.
